claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. My son Alex is 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to assess Alex's eligibility.

**Does Alex live with you?** Or does he live with someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you. I need to gather a bit more information about Alex's circumstances.

**Is Alex in full-time education or training?** For example, is he attending school, college, or an approved training programme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He actually just left school recently, but he's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. That's helpful information.

**Is Alex currently in any form of full-time education, training, or an apprenticeship?** Or is he between school and his next step right now with no formal programme in place yet?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's between school and his next step right now - no formal programme in place yet. He's just working with the careers service to explore his options.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I need to check one more important detail.

**Has Alex reached his 16th birthday?** You mentioned he's 16 years old, but I need to confirm - has he already had his 16th birthday, or is he still awaiting it?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's already had his 16th birthday.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me gather the remaining details I need.

**Since Alex left school, has he been registered with an approved education or training provider** (such as being registered for a course, apprenticeship, or training scheme), **or is he currently only in contact with the careers service without being enrolled in a formal programme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's currently only in contact with the careers service - he's not enrolled in any formal programme or course yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for all that information. Before I make my final assessment, let me check the eligibility rules to ensure I give you an accurate answer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I've reviewed the eligibility rules. Based on the information you've provided, I can now make my assessment.

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if your child is 16 or over **and they stay in approved education or training**. However, there's an important provision: **you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service**.

Since Alex is 16, has left school, and is now registered with the local careers service (which is a government-sponsored careers service), he qualifies for the 20-week extension period. This means you **are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**, but only for a 20-week period from when he registered with the careers service.

It's important to note that after this 20-week period ends, Alex will need to either:
- Enter approved education or training, or
- Start work (though if it's 24+ hours per week without being in education/training, eligibility would stop)

for you to continue receiving Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: **Summary:** You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex for a period of 20 weeks from when he registered with the careers service. Make sure to apply within this timeframe to secure this extension!
